devdoc.author: Ronan Sandford
devdoc.details: The router's own code is its compiled runtime code with its immutables, so every block  explorer verifies it, Etherscan included. Reading the data contract costs a cold account access  (EIP-2929) on the first read of a transaction, about 2,600 gas, which `InlineRouter` saves by  keeping the routes in its own code (verified by Sourcify and Blockscout, not by Etherscan).
devdoc.title: Router for up to 256 implementations and about 1,460 selectors, verifiable anywhere

userdoc.notice: Create an immutable route and delegate function calls to their respective  implementations. The routes are checked at construction (see `RouterRoutes.check`) and kept  in a data contract the router creates (its code: a STOP, then the implementations, 20 bytes  each, then the sig map, 5 bytes an entry), which a lookup binary-searches with EXTCODECOPY.  The limit is what a deployment can carry: on a chain with EIP-3860 (Shanghai and later), about  1,460 selectors, since the constructor takes the routes ABI-encoded (32 bytes a selector) and  init code is at most 49,152 bytes there; elsewhere about 4,900, under EIP-170's 24,576 bytes  of code for the data contract.
